claims.text: Increasing Al concentration in CrFeCoNiX can create a distinct Al-rich reservoir phase.
An Al-rich reservoir phase can provide a sustained supply of Al to the alloy surface by slow diffusion.
Outward Al diffusion promotes surface Al2O3 formation.
A continuous supply of Al enables formation of a dense, continuous, and coherent Al2O3 scale.
The Al2O3 scale maintains adhesion by mitigating oxidation-induced stress and crack formation.
An Al-rich reservoir will produce an Al2O3 scale that resists cracking and spalling above 900 °C.
The protective Al2O3 scale will grow slowly during prolonged high-temperature oxidation.
The modified alloy will form a more continuous and mechanically robust Al2O3 scale than a lower-Al baseline.
Standard lower-Al CrFeCoNiX alloys are more prone to forming unstable oxide scales that crack or spall.
Oxidation of CrFeCoNiMn at 900–1100 °C involves composition-dependent layered oxides and outward cation transport.
The hypothesis applies in both oxidizing and corrosive environments above 900 °C.
The mechanism applies to both single-phase and multiphase solid-solution states if an Al-rich reservoir is distinguishable.
Internal oxidation and phase-boundary oxidation can contribute to embrittlement, microcracking, and scale spallation.
A 950 °C, 100-hour controlled oxidation comparison can test the proposed reservoir mechanism.
Failure of the modified alloy to show a more continuous, coherent, and slow-growing Al2O3 scale than the control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention requires formation of a distinct Al-rich reservoir phase, which makes the modified microstructure multiphase, while the boundary states that the mechanism is applicable to single-phase states when such a distinct phase is present.

The central hypothesis specifically predicts protection in oxidative atmospheres, whereas the conditions and boundary extend the claim to unspecified corrosive atmospheres without identifying the corrosive species or a mechanism applicable to them.
